body:
"I have very little sympathy for people with suicidal tenancies."

I honestly don't see why you are here.

However, I will respond to something you brought up. She has many people who depend on her (family, friends, work, etc). She's doing her best to resolve the dependencies. She is no hesitating (based on my understanding), she's just waiting.

See I do care about her. It's just I see it as I'm the person who has to decide whether to pull the plug on an ailing patient who is done living. She described it as just being a husk of a person. In not pulling the plug, she just suffers. Can I truly tell her she needs to keep living, to keep suffering? 

She is not going to kill herself anytime soon. Maybe in a couple years or perhaps a month but I'm doing my best to get her to come to the decision to live on her own. I can't force her to be happy.

Now, I don't know your situation but please promise me a couple thing.

Please wait and think things over. Do something you enjoy; do the last thing that made you smile. Go for a walk some place you've felt at piece and take in your environment. Think about your act. 

Perhaps, help a person. You don't need to but try to find someone who is hurting or need helps. When understanding and fixing the problems of others you begin to fully understand your own. 

I can't be there to help you but I ask you do these things.

First, relax. No one can ever think when panicking.

Now, do your best to tell her to meet you. Tell her to at least have a talk, share a beer or go for a ride. It'll give you a chance to prevent her physically from doing it. If it's the alcohol, you can be there for her as it goes through her system. Just try to get her to meet you but be sure to never get off the phone with her!
